findings.issue_text: [BUG] NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) but the surrounding function scope (per the hunk, which declares no ctx and does not change the NewResourceServer(opts ResourceServerOptions) signature) provides no ctx variable, so the package fails to compile with 'undefined: ctx'. go build of pkg/storage/unified/resource breaks; the entire PR cannot be built or tested until ctx is threaded in (e.g. context.Background()) or added to the signature, which in turn breaks every existing caller of NewResourceServer.

[ADVISORY] The postgres path of the storage-server integration test is now unconditionally skipped with a TODO ('test not working with postgres in Drone'), leaving the unified storage server's main production DB backend with zero CI coverage. Regressions in the resource server's init-on-startup path and SQL backend against postgres (the backend this very PR touches in pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go) will pass CI green; anyone running Drone or postgres gets broken behavior discovered only in production.

[ADVISORY] Dropping the cacheMu-held critical section from the whole of BuildIndex removes the serialization that previously prevented two concurrent builds of the same NamespacedResource, and for file-backed indexes both builders now call bleve.New on the same directory path. Concurrent index builds for one key race on the filesystem dir and on the b.cache map write; bleve.New on an already-populated dir returns an error, so the loser returns an index-build failure and the winner's cache entry can be overwritten by a stale, lower-RV index — search results silently lose documents until rebuild.

[ADVISORY] Init is moved from lazy per-request (where a transient backend failure surfaced as a single failed request or health check) into NewResourceServer, making any init failure a hard construction/startup failure. Operators whose search-index build or watcher init hits a transient DB error at boot now get a process that refuses to start, instead of a degraded server that retries Init on the next request — a failure that was per-request becomes a hard startup failure, and IsHealthy can no longer report initErr because the server is never constructed.

[BUG] Removing the per-request s.Init(ctx) guards and calling Init only in NewResourceServer converts every lazy-init failure into a hard construction failure, but Init remains exported and other constructors/paths (any caller that builds a server without going through this branch, or that hits initErr from the sync.Once-style path) now race with requests that were previously self-healing. If NewResourceServer is invoked with a ctx that is already cancelled/expired (e.g. a request-scoped ctx), Init fails and the server can never be constructed, whereas the old code allowed later requests with fresh contexts to retry initialization; conversely any caller still relying on the per-method Init retry gets a server whose initErr is never re-attempted and whose methods now return uninitialized-store errors (nil search, no watcher) instead of triggering init.

[BUG] Reordering initWatcher to run after search.init means events written between snapshot query and watcher start are silently dropped from the search index. A dashboard saved during the (potentially minutes-long) index build is missed by the watcher and absent from the snapshot query that ran before it, leaving the search index permanently stale for that resource until a full rebuild; the old order (watcher first) captured those events.

[BUG] Dropping the cacheMu lock held across BuildIndex allows two concurrent callers of getOrCreateIndex for the same NamespacedResource to both build and register an index, with the last writer to b.cache[key] winning and the loser's file-based bleve index (opened on disk under opts.Root) leaked. Concurrent first-time access to the same resource type opens two bleve indices on the same directory; the loser's index handle is dropped without Close, leaking file handles and, on file-backed indexes, leaving two writers to the same dir; also the caller that receives the orphaned index serves a stale index that never receives cache updates from subsequent builds.

[ADVISORY] The only test change in this PR is skipping the postgres integration test with a TODO, so the reordered Init sequence, the eager-init failure path, and the new concurrency in bleve BuildIndex ship with zero new verification. The postgres storage-server integration coverage is silently dropped (CI goes green on a DB backend the diff's server.go changes directly affect), and the init-reordering/watcher-skew behavior has no spec; operators on postgres get regressions that CI cannot catch.

[ADVISORY] History and Origin call s.search.History/Origin with no nil check, and previously their per-method Init guaranteed the search support was initialized before use; after moving Init to construction, any server constructed without search configured (s.search == nil — a supported configuration, as Search itself checks for it) panics with nil pointer dereference on History/Origin. A deployment with search disabled that issues a History or Origin RPC crashes the handler with a nil-pointer panic instead of returning the error the old Init-guarded path produced.

[BUG] NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously, converting previously lazy per-request initialization into a hard construction-time failure. Any consumer constructing the resource server (including the integration test that the diff then skips for postgres with a TODO) gets a nil server / error at startup when index building fails, where previously requests failed individually with a retry path; NewResourceServer also has no documented requirement demanding eager init, so this is scope drift beyond 'performance optimization' that changes failure semantics for all callers.

[BUG] Reordering search.init before initWatcher means index build now races against a not-yet-started watcher instead of watcher-before-index. Events written between watcher start and the (now later) index build snapshot are lost from the index until a rebuild, or events during the (now longer pre-watcher) index build are never captured; either ordering has a gap, but the diff changes which gap exists without any requirement tracing this reorder, and the integration test that would catch regressions here is skipped in the same PR.

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the start of BuildIndex lets two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key both run bleve.New on the same on-disk directory. Two concurrent builders for the same namespace/resource key race writing the same bleve directory (file-threshold path), corrupting or erroring the persistent index; the lock was narrowed to only the cache write, so the whole build is no longer serialized per key. This is a correctness change smuggled into a performance PR with no requirement tracing it.

[ADVISORY] The PR permanently skips the storage-server integration test for postgres with a TODO instead of fixing it. The exact behavior this PR changes (eager Init at construction, watcher/search ordering) loses its only integration coverage on a primary database backend; regressions on postgres ship undetected, and the skip has no issue link or removal condition.

[ADVISORY] Init guards were stripped from every RPC method (Read, List, Search, History, Origin, Watch, blobs) based solely on the single call added in NewResourceServer, but the server struct is exported and Init is a public method, so any path that constructs the server without NewResourceServer (or calls Init again) now serves requests against an uninitialized watcher/search. Any out-of-tree or future constructor path (e.g., tests, alternate wiring) that builds the server struct directly serves RPCs with nil watcher/search state instead of getting the previous Init error; the removed guards were the invariant enforcing 'no request before init' and nothing in this diff re-establishes it for non-NewResourceServer construction.

[BUG] Removing the per-request Init(ctx) checks means that when background initialization fails (s.initErr set inside Init's goroutine), every RPC handler — Read, List, Search, Watch, History, Create, Update, Delete — now executes against an uninitialized server instead of returning the init error. A transient DB failure during index build permanently poisons the server via the cached initErr, but callers no longer see it: they get silently wrong/empty results (no watcher running, no search index, List serving raw backend state) rather than the error the old contract promised.

[BUG] Calling s.Init(ctx) inside NewResourceServer converts a previously lazy, per-request failure into a hard construction failure with no retry or degradation path. If index building fails at construction (e.g. bleve file creation error or backend unreachable at boot), NewResourceServer returns an error and the whole process fails to start, where previously the server started and only the affected requests failed; also the ctx passed at construction may already be cancelled/short-lived depending on the caller, aborting a startup that previously used the request-scoped context.

[BUG] Reordering so search index build runs before initWatcher means write events that occur during the (potentially long) index build are never delivered to the search index. Previously the watcher was started first so events during build were consumed; now any Create/Update/Delete landing between the DB snapshot used by build and initWatcher's start is permanently missing from the index until that resource is written again — stale search results with no error anywhere.

[ADVISORY] Moving the cacheMu.Lock() from the start of BuildIndex to just before the cache write removes the mutual exclusion that previously serialized concurrent index builds for the same key. Two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource now both construct a full bleve index (doubling memory/CPU and file I/O) and the loser's documents/index object is discarded while any handle already obtained to it keeps a dead index; safe only if getOrCreateIndex's own locking serializes calls, which the diff does not show.

[ADVISORY] Skipping the integration test for postgres with a 'works locally' TODO is a stand-in guard: CI goes green while the primary production database path for the instrumentation server is untested. Postgres-specific regressions in the storage server bootstrap path (exactly the code this PR changes — eager Init at construction) ship undetected; the skip may itself be masking a real postgres failure this diff introduces.

[ADVISORY] The diff moves Init from per-request lazy invocation to a hard call inside NewResourceServer, converting a per-request recoverable failure into a constructor failure under a PR titled 'Performance Optimizations' — a semantic change to the server's failure contract that was not part of the stated objective. Operators embedding NewResourceServer (e.g. in tests or alternative binaries) who previously got a server that served requests even when search/index initialization failed, or failed per-request with a retry on the next call, now get no server at all from the constructor; any transient init failure (e.g. DB hiccup during index build) becomes a fatal startup error with no retry path, since all per-method Init calls were deleted too.

[ADVISORY] The diff reorders initWatcher to run after search index initialization, silently changing which events are captured versus the original design. If any code path still reaches Init later (it is a public method and still performs the same sequence), or if the watcher previously caught writes emitted during index build, resource versions written between the end of s.search.init and the start of s.initWatcher are never delivered to the index, leaving the search index permanently stale for those documents until a restart; the ordering change is a correctness-behavior change shipped under a performance-only PR title with no stated acceptance.

[ADVISORY] The diff silently disables the only integration test for the instrumentation server against postgres with a TODO, changing the verified contract of this PR from 'works against supported databases' to 'verified only locally'. CI passes while postgres regressions in the storage server path go undetected; the TODO has no tracked follow-up, so the exclusion persists indefinitely and anyone relying on Drone greenness as acceptance is being told the feature is tested when it is not.

[ADVISORY] History and Origin now call s.search.History / s.search.Origin unconditionally after removing the Init guard, but unlike Search they lack a nil check on s.search. When a server is constructed without search configured (s.search == nil, the same configuration Search at line 919 explicitly guards against), History and Origin now panic with a nil-pointer dereference instead of returning the previous Init error or a proper error — a regression introduced by removing the guard without auditing all call sites it protected.

[ADVISORY] The diff permanently disables the postgres integration test path with a TODO comment ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.'), removing the only CI coverage for the storage server on postgres while simultaneously changing the server's initialization contract. The same PR moves Init() from every RPC handler into NewResourceServer (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:255-260), making init failures a hard constructor error instead of a per-request error. That behavioral change is exactly the kind of startup-path change this integration test was positioned to catch, yet its postgres coverage is being switched off in the same diff with no replacement test, no linked issue, and no timeout on the TODO — postgres regressions in server init will ship undetected.

[ADVISORY] Lazy per-request initialization is moved into NewResourceServer, converting what was previously a per-request failure into a hard startup failure. A Grafana operator whose search-index backend (bleve dir on disk, DB stats query in GetResourceStats) has a transient problem at boot now gets a server that refuses to start entirely, instead of a server that serves Create/Read/List/Watch and returns errors only for search until init recovers; previously-failing init also can never be retried since Init is no longer invoked lazily by any handler.

[ADVISORY] GetResourceStats' span context is now propagated into the traced query path, tying index-build data scans to the request that triggered construction rather than a detached background ctx from the first API call. Minor: trace/cancellation semantics of the index build changed with no accompanying test; during the now-constructor-time Init this is fine, but callers of Init(ctx) embedders pass an arbitrary ctx whose cancellation now aborts stats queries mid-scan.

[ADVISORY] Removing the BuildIndex-wide cacheMu lock allows two concurrent index builds for the same NamespacedResource to both create a bleve index at the same on-disk directory filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", key.Resource, key.Group)). Concurrent builders for the same key race writing the same bleve directory (file corruption / index opening errors) and the later b.cache[key] = idx last-write-wins discards one builder's resource-version bookkeeping; previously the whole-function lock serialized builds. Whoever gets bitten: any path that triggers two simultaneous cold-start builds of the same resource type — now more likely since server.go's Init moved into construction while other entrypoints (getOrCreateIndex on cache miss) can still race a slow build.

[ADVISORY] Init order changed so the search index is fully built before initWatcher starts, leaving an uncovered gap where writes completing during the (potentially minutes-long) index build produce no WrittenEvent, so those resource versions are permanently missing from the search index. Dashboards created/updated during the startup index build are silently unfindable via search until the next full rebuild or a write that re-triggers an event for the same key; the old order (watcher first, then index build) ensured events for concurrent writes were queued/handled. Users searching for a just-created dashboard get no results — silent data omission from the index, not an error.

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock for the duration of BuildIndex allows concurrent builds of the same key to run in parallel, with two bleve.New(dir) calls targeting the same on-disk directory. Two requests that miss the cache for the same NamespacedResource simultaneously both construct an index at the same filepath (bleve.New on the same dir), corrupting or failing one of the on-disk indexes; the cache then does last-write-wins, so the surviving in-memory index may reference the corrupted directory. Previously the full-build lock serialized this.

[ADVISORY] Init is now invoked synchronously inside NewResourceServer, converting previously per-request, per-callsite lazy initialization into a hard construction-time failure. Any transient failure during search index bootstrap (which the code itself documents as potentially slow and now logs a duration for) or watcher setup prevents the resource server from being constructed at all, so the entire process fails startup instead of the previous behavior where only the affected requests returned errors and other operations could proceed; operators on multi-tenant deployments get an all-or-nothing boot for one tenant's bad index.

[ADVISORY] With the Init call removed from History and Origin, these methods dereference s.search with no nil guard, while Search retains an explicit 'search index not configured' check. If NewResourceServer is constructed without a search support configured (a non-error condition per Init, which only initializes search when s.search != nil), History and Origin return a nil-pointer panic / 500 to the API caller instead of the typed 'search index not configured' error the sibling Search endpoint returns — a wrong-shape response on a reachable path.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (server.go:255+), while the previous lazy per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from RPC handlers including `IsHealthy` (server.go:446-, 488-, 542-, 634-, 693-, 786-, 930-, 941-, 971-, 1016-). This means an init failure (e.g., watcher/search init) becomes a construction/startup failure rather than a per-request failure that could be retried on subsequent requests/health checks. That’s a concrete operational/behavioral change grounded in the diff, though not provably a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the per-request s.Init(ctx) guards and calling Init only in NewResourceServer converts every lazy-init failure into a hard construction failure, but Init remains exported and other constructors/paths (any caller that builds a server without going through this branch, or that hits initErr from the sync.Once-style path) now race with requests that were previously self-healing. adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a behavioral change: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on init failure, and all per-method `s.Init(ctx)` guards were removed (e.g., `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...`). That can be an API/initialization-semantics concern for callers that previously could construct the server even if init would later fail. However, the finding’s claim that the old code was “self-healing”/could “retry initialization with fresh contexts” is not supported by the diff because `Init` uses a `sync.Once`-style `s.initOnce.Do(...)`, so a failed first init would not be retried anyway. Assertions about other constructors/paths are also not verifiable from the diff alone.

A dashboard saved during the (potentially minutes-long) index build is missed by the watcher and absent from the snapshot query that ran before it, leaving the search index permanently stale for that resource until a full rebuild; the old order (watcher first) captured those events.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go, Init() now runs `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (the watcher start was moved below search index initialization). If `search.init` performs a point-in-time scan/build of the index (as implied by its “index initialized” logging and timing) and the watcher is responsible for incrementally applying subsequent events, this reordering creates a gap where writes occurring during the (potentially long) index build are neither included in the initial snapshot build nor observed by the watcher (since it hasn’t started yet). The old order (watcher first) reduced/avoided that missed-events window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Dropping the cacheMu lock held across BuildIndex allows two concurrent callers of getOrCreateIndex for the same NamespacedResource to both build and register an index, with the last writer to b.cache[key] winning and the loser's file-based bleve index (opened on disk under opts.Root) leaked. Concurrent first-time access to the same resource type opens two bleve indices on the same directory; the loser's index handle is dropped without Close, leaking file handles and, on file-backed indexes, leaving two writers to the same dir; also the caller that receives the orphaned index serves a stale index that never receives cache updates from subsequent builds.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire method (covering cache check/build/open and cache write). The diff removes that coarse lock and only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. From the diff alone, nothing else is shown that prevents two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same `key` from both creating/opening a bleve index (including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` for file-backed indexes) and then racing to store into `b.cache`. That can leave an extra index instance not tracked in `b.cache` (and no Close is performed here), which is a real resource-leak / correctness risk introduced by this change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a TODO skip for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer`, reducing CI coverage for postgres. Meanwhile, nontrivial behavior changes land in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go` (eager `s.Init(ctx)` in `NewResourceServer`, removal of per-RPC `Init` calls, and reordering search init vs watcher start) and in `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go` (removing the broad `cacheMu` lock around `BuildIndex`, changing concurrency characteristics). No new or adjusted tests are added to validate these behavioral/concurrency/init-order changes, so the review concern about dropped verification is diff-grounded (though claims about actual regressions are speculative).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] History and Origin call s.search.History/Origin with no nil check, and previously their per-method Init guaranteed the search support was initialized before use; after moving Init to construction, any server constructed without search configured (s.search == nil — a supported configuration, as Search itself checks for it) panics with nil pointer dereference on History/Origin. A deployment with search disabled that issues a History or Origin RPC crashes the handler with a nil-pointer panic instead of returning the error the old Init-guarded path produced.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, History and Origin previously called s.Init(ctx) but still unconditionally returned s.search.History/Origin; there was no nil-check before either. s.Init(ctx) (as shown) only initializes the search index if s.search != nil and does not create/configure s.search, so it could not have “guaranteed” non-nil search support nor produced an error for a nil search configuration. Therefore the claimed regression (“after moving Init to construction … panics instead of returning the old Init-guarded error”) is not supported by the diff; the nil-deref risk would have existed before as well if History/Origin were called with s.search == nil.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), while many RPC handlers no longer call `s.Init(ctx)` per request (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). This is a diff-grounded behavioral/compatibility concern (eager construction-time failure vs previously deferring init errors to request time), but the diff alone does not prove it is an incorrect behavior/"bug" rather than an intentional design change. Parts of the finding tying this to the postgres test skip and a specific prior "retry path" are not directly verifiable from the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Reordering search.init before initWatcher means index build now races against a not-yet-started watcher instead of watcher-before-index. Events written between watcher start and the (now later) index build snapshot are lost from the index until a rebuild, or events during the (now longer pre-watcher) index build are never captured; either ordering has a gap, but the diff changes which gap exists without any requirement tracing this reorder, and the integration test that would catch regressions here is skipped in the same PR.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably reorders initialization in `(*server).Init`: previously it started the watcher (`s.initWatcher()`) before building the search index (`s.search.init(ctx)`), and now it builds the index first and starts the watcher afterward. That creates a concrete, diff-grounded concern about a “missed events” window during index initialization if writes can occur concurrently (e.g., from other processes) before the watcher is active. The PR also adds a `t.Skip` for postgres in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer`, reducing coverage that might catch related regressions. However, the diff alone doesn’t show the watcher/indexing semantics needed to prove actual data loss, so this can’t be confirmed as a definite bug solely from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the start of BuildIndex lets two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key both run bleve.New on the same on-disk directory. This is a correctness change smuggled into a performance PR with no requirement tracing it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go removes the b.cacheMu lock that previously serialized the entire BuildIndex call and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This unquestionably changes concurrency behavior: multiple goroutines can now run the expensive/index-creating section concurrently. However, from the diff alone we cannot verify that BuildIndex is ever called concurrently for the same `key`, nor that `bleve.New(dir, ...)` will corrupt/error if invoked concurrently on the same directory. So the finding’s specific corruption claim isn’t directly verifiable from this PR, but the narrowed lock is a concrete, diff-grounded concurrency/correctness risk worth flagging.

The exact behavior this PR changes (eager Init at construction, watcher/search ordering) loses its only integration coverage on a primary database backend; regressions on postgres ship undetected, and the skip has no issue link or removal condition.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a new unconditional skip for postgres in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (`if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip("skipping - test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.") }`) with only a TODO comment and no issue/cleanup condition. In the same PR, nontrivial behavior changes occur in the storage server (e.g., `NewResourceServer` now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` and `Init` changes watcher/search init ordering), so skipping postgres reduces integration coverage on a primary backend for these changes. This is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern but not itself a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init guards were stripped from every RPC method (Read, List, Search, History, Origin, Watch, blobs) based solely on the single call added in NewResourceServer, but the server struct is exported and Init is a public method, so any path that constructs the server without NewResourceServer (or calls Init again) now serves requests against an uninitialized watcher/search. Any out-of-tree or future constructor path (e.g., tests, alternate wiring) that builds the server struct directly serves RPCs with nil watcher/search state instead of getting the previous Init error; the removed guards were the invariant enforcing 'no request before init' and nothing in this diff re-establishes it for non-NewResourceServer construction.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` guards across many methods (Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/blobs, etc.) and instead calls `s.Init(ctx)` once in `NewResourceServer` (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go). That does change the invariant from “lazy init on first request” to “must be initialized at construction,” and there is no fallback if a `*server` is created without going through `NewResourceServer`. However, the finding overstates this as a concrete defect: the concrete type is `type server` (unexported, receiver `(s *server)`), so out-of-package construction is not supported by the diff; the risk mainly applies to in-package alternate wiring/tests. This is a real maintainability/robustness concern introduced by the change, but not a verifiable broken behavior from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the per-request Init(ctx) checks means that when background initialization fails (s.initErr set inside Init's goroutine), every RPC handler — Read, List, Search, Watch, History, Create, Update, Delete — now executes against an uninitialized server instead of returning the init error. A transient DB failure during index build permanently poisons the server via the cached initErr, but callers no longer see it: they get silently wrong/empty results (no watcher running, no search index, List serving raw backend state) rather than the error the old contract promised.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` from essentially all RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob). Although `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` once and returns an error if that call fails immediately, `server.Init` is structured around setting `s.initErr` during its internal initialization flow (the shown code mutates `s.initErr` and logs errors inside the init path). With the per-request calls removed, there is no longer any handler-level check that surfaces a later-populated `s.initErr` to callers. If initialization happens asynchronously or can fail after `NewResourceServer` returns (consistent with the finding’s mention of an init goroutine and with the code mutating `s.initErr` during init steps like `s.search.init(ctx)` / `s.initWatcher()`), RPCs can proceed without returning the init failure, changing behavior from “fail fast on init error” to “serve requests despite init failure.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Calling s.Init(ctx) inside NewResourceServer converts a previously lazy, per-request failure into a hard construction failure with no retry or degradation path. If index building fails at construction (e.g. bleve file creation error or backend unreachable at boot), NewResourceServer returns an error and the whole process fails to start, where previously the server started and only the affected requests failed; also the ctx passed at construction may already be cancelled/short-lived depending on the caller, aborting a startup that previously used the request-scoped context.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `err := s.Init(ctx)` in `NewResourceServer` and returns the error (`return nil, err`) on init failure, while removing the per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls from all RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). This is a clear behavioral change from lazy initialization on first request to eager initialization during construction, which can now fail server creation/startup if `Init` (including `s.search.init(ctx)` and `s.initWatcher()`) errors. The claim about the construction `ctx` being cancelled/short-lived is not verifiable from the shown diff because the origin/lifetime of `ctx` in `NewResourceServer` is not included.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Reordering so search index build runs before initWatcher means write events that occur during the (potentially long) index build are never delivered to the search index. Previously the watcher was started first so events during build were consumed; now any Create/Update/Delete landing between the DB snapshot used by build and initWatcher's start is permanently missing from the index until that resource is written again — stale search results with no error anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: In server.Init, the diff moves `s.search.init(ctx)` (which builds/initializes the search index) to run before `s.initWatcher()` (diff shows watcher start block moved below index init). If the watcher is the mechanism that feeds `WrittenEvent`s into the search index (`handleEvent`), then any writes occurring while `search.init` is running will not be observed by the watcher (since it hasn’t started yet). Unless `search.init`/`initWatcher` have an explicit catch-up/high-watermark mechanism (not shown in this diff), this creates a real window where changes can be missed, resulting in a stale index with no error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Moving the cacheMu.Lock() from the start of BuildIndex to just before the cache write removes the mutual exclusion that previously serialized concurrent index builds for the same key. Two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource now both construct a full bleve index (doubling memory/CPU and file I/O) and the loser's documents/index object is discarded while any handle already obtained to it keeps a dead index; safe only if getOrCreateIndex's own locking serializes calls, which the diff does not show.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for the entire build; the diff removes that and only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This undeniably removes backend-level serialization of concurrent index builds, so two goroutines could concurrently construct separate bleve indexes for the same key (including potentially targeting the same on-disk `dir`), wasting CPU/I/O and making the cache winner nondeterministic. However, the diff does not show the caller’s concurrency control (e.g., `getOrCreateIndex`), so it’s not verifiable from the diff alone that this becomes a correctness defect in practice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Skipping the integration test for postgres with a 'works locally' TODO is a stand-in guard: CI goes green while the primary production database path for the instrumentation server is untested. Postgres-specific regressions in the storage server bootstrap path (exactly the code this PR changes — eager Init at construction) ship undetected; the skip may itself be masking a real postgres failure this diff introduces.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a postgres-specific skip in an integration test with a "Works locally" TODO (pkg/server/module_server_test.go), which will make CI green while not exercising the postgres path. In the same PR, initialization behavior changes materially: NewResourceServer now eagerly calls s.Init(ctx) and the per-RPC Init calls are removed (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go). Skipping postgres means this new bootstrap/Init-at-construction behavior is not covered for a major DB backend, which is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a provable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff moves Init from per-request lazy invocation to a hard call inside NewResourceServer, converting a per-request recoverable failure into a constructor failure under a PR titled 'Performance Optimizations' — a semantic change to the server's failure contract that was not part of the stated objective. Operators embedding NewResourceServer (e.g. in tests or alternative binaries) who previously got a server that served requests even when search/index initialization failed, or failed per-request with a retry on the next call, now get no server at all from the constructor; any transient init failure (e.g. DB hiccup during index build) becomes a fatal startup error with no retry path, since all per-method Init calls were deleted too.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if it fails (server.go: `err := s.Init(ctx); if err != nil { ... return nil, err }`), while all the previous per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls in methods like `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...` were removed. This is a real, diff-grounded contract change (eager/fatal init vs lazy/per-request init). However, the finding’s claims about a prior "retry on the next call" or "served requests even when search/index initialization failed" are not fully verifiable from the diff alone (e.g., `Init` likely uses `sync.Once` / `initErr` which may prevent retries anyway), making it more of a scope/architecture concern than a provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff reorders initWatcher to run after search index initialization, silently changing which events are captured versus the original design. If any code path still reaches Init later (it is a public method and still performs the same sequence), or if the watcher previously caught writes emitted during index build, resource versions written between the end of s.search.init and the start of s.initWatcher are never delivered to the index, leaving the search index permanently stale for those documents until a restart; the ordering change is a correctness-behavior change shipped under a performance-only PR title with no stated acceptance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably reorder initialization: in `server.Init` the watcher startup (`s.initWatcher()`) was moved to run *after* `s.search.init(ctx)` (previously watcher started first). That creates a real, diff-grounded behavioral change (a gap where writes could occur before the watcher is active). However, the finding’s stronger claim that this will “never” deliver those events and “permanently” stale the index cannot be proven from the diff alone (it depends on whether any writes can occur concurrently during init and whether other mechanisms reconcile missed events). The new `NewResourceServer` now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` and per-RPC `Init` calls were removed, which likely reduces the window, but does not eliminate the architectural concern introduced by the reordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff silently disables the only integration test for the instrumentation server against postgres with a TODO, changing the verified contract of this PR from 'works against supported databases' to 'verified only locally'. CI passes while postgres regressions in the storage server path go undetected; the TODO has no tracked follow-up, so the exclusion persists indefinitely and anyone relying on Drone greenness as acceptance is being told the feature is tested when it is not.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional skip for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (`pkg/server/module_server_test.go`), with only a TODO comment. This reduces CI coverage for postgres for that integration scenario and can allow regressions to pass undetected. While the finding’s claim that it is the *only* such integration test and that it changes a broader “works against supported databases” contract cannot be fully verified from this diff alone, the test-disablement itself is explicitly present and is a concrete review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] History and Origin now call s.search.History / s.search.Origin unconditionally after removing the Init guard, but unlike Search they lack a nil check on s.search. When a server is constructed without search configured (s.search == nil, the same configuration Search at line 919 explicitly guards against), History and Origin now panic with a nil-pointer dereference instead of returning the previous Init error or a proper error — a regression introduced by removing the guard without auditing all call sites it protected.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go, Search now explicitly guards `if s.search == nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("search index not configured") }` (around the shown Search method), but History and Origin were changed to remove the `s.Init(ctx)` guard and still call `return s.search.History(ctx, req)` / `return s.search.Origin(ctx, req)` with no `s.search` nil check. If the server is configured without search (`s.search == nil`), these methods will dereference nil and panic. While the finding’s claim about “previous Init error” isn’t provable from this diff (Init doesn’t create `s.search`), the nil-deref risk in History/Origin is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff permanently disables the postgres integration test path with a TODO comment ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.'), removing the only CI coverage for the storage server on postgres while simultaneously changing the server's initialization contract. The same PR moves Init() from every RPC handler into NewResourceServer (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:255-260), making init failures a hard constructor error instead of a per-request error. That behavioral change is exactly the kind of startup-path change this integration test was positioned to catch, yet its postgres coverage is being switched off in the same diff with no replacement test, no linked issue, and no timeout on the TODO — postgres regressions in server init will ship undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a postgres skip to an integration test with a TODO note (pkg/server/module_server_test.go) which removes postgres CI coverage for that path. In the same PR, Init() is moved from being invoked in each RPC handler to being invoked during NewResourceServer construction (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), changing init failures from per-request errors to constructor-time errors. Disabling postgres coverage while changing the initialization contract is a concrete, diff-grounded testing/coverage risk, but not a directly verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Lazy per-request initialization is moved into NewResourceServer, converting what was previously a per-request failure into a hard startup failure. A Grafana operator whose search-index backend (bleve dir on disk, DB stats query in GetResourceStats) has a transient problem at boot now gets a server that refuses to start entirely, instead of a server that serves Create/Read/List/Watch and returns errors only for search until init recovers; previously-failing init also can never be retried since Init is no longer invoked lazily by any handler.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move initialization from per-RPC handlers into construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if it fails (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), while the `Init(ctx)` calls were removed from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc. This does convert certain init-time failures (e.g., search index init, watcher init) from “server starts but RPCs error” into “server creation fails / startup fails”, which is a real operational/architecture concern. However, the finding’s claim that previously Create/Read/List/Watch would continue working while only search failed isn’t supported by the diff: previously *all* those handlers returned early on `Init` error. Also, `Init` appears guarded by a once/do pattern (not shown here but implied by `s.initErr`/ordering), so “init can never be retried” was likely already true; what changes is that handlers no longer trigger `Init` at all.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] GetResourceStats' span context is now propagated into the traced query path, tying index-build data scans to the request that triggered construction rather than a detached background ctx from the first API call. Minor: trace/cancellation semantics of the index build changed with no accompanying test; during the now-constructor-time Init this is fine, but callers of Init(ctx) embedders pass an arbitrary ctx whose cancellation now aborts stats queries mid-scan.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `GetResourceStats` from `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)` to `ctx, span := ...` (pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go), meaning downstream work in that method now runs with the span-derived context. That’s a behavioral change in tracing propagation (and potentially deadline/cancellation handling for any subcalls that use the `ctx` variable), and the diff shows no accompanying test/guard around the new semantics. However, the finding’s more specific claims about “detached background ctx from the first API call” and index-build/query linkage aren’t directly verifiable from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the BuildIndex-wide cacheMu lock allows two concurrent index builds for the same NamespacedResource to both create a bleve index at the same on-disk directory filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", key.Resource, key.Group)). Concurrent builders for the same key race writing the same bleve directory (file corruption / index opening errors) and the later b.cache[key] = idx last-write-wins discards one builder's resource-version bookkeeping; previously the whole-function lock serialized builds. Whoever gets bitten: any path that triggers two simultaneous cold-start builds of the same resource type — now more likely since server.go's Init moved into construction while other entrypoints (getOrCreateIndex on cache miss) can still race a slow build.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function but now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. The on-disk index path for `size > b.opts.FileThreshold` is deterministically derived from `key` (`filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", ...))`), so concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same `key` can both execute `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` against the same directory with no serialization. The diff no longer prevents that race (and the cache update becomes last-write-wins), which can plausibly cause index creation/open errors or corrupt the directory under concurrent builds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init order changed so the search index is fully built before initWatcher starts, leaving an uncovered gap where writes completing during the (potentially minutes-long) index build produce no WrittenEvent, so those resource versions are permanently missing from the search index. Dashboards created/updated during the startup index build are silently unfindable via search until the next full rebuild or a write that re-triggers an event for the same key; the old order (watcher first, then index build) ensured events for concurrent writes were queued/handled. Users searching for a just-created dashboard get no results — silent data omission from the index, not an error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change init order: in `(*server).Init`, search index initialization (`s.search.init(ctx)`) now runs before starting the watcher (`s.initWatcher()`), whereas previously the watcher started first (see the moved blocks around `Init` in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`). If `initWatcher` is the only source of `WrittenEvent`s and it does not replay/catch up from a known resource version, this order could leave a window where writes occurring during the (potentially long) index build are not observed and thus not indexed. However, the diff alone does not show `initWatcher` semantics (e.g., whether it backfills/replays) nor whether writes can occur during init (notably `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` synchronously before returning), so the “permanent missing docs” behavior cannot be conclusively verified from this patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock for the duration of BuildIndex allows concurrent builds of the same key to run in parallel, with two bleve.New(dir) calls targeting the same on-disk directory. Two requests that miss the cache for the same NamespacedResource simultaneously both construct an index at the same filepath (bleve.New on the same dir), corrupting or failing one of the on-disk indexes; the cache then does last-write-wins, so the surviving in-memory index may reference the corrupted directory. Previously the full-build lock serialized this.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire build (including bleve.New(dir, ...) / bleve.NewMemOnly and builder execution). The diff removes that broad lock and now only locks around the final b.cache[key] = idx assignment. From the diff alone, this change allows concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key to run in parallel and both compute the same on-disk directory path (filepath.Join(... key.Namespace ... key.Resource ... key.Group)), meaning two goroutines can call bleve.New(dir, ...) against the same directory concurrently. That can lead to failures/corruption and a last-writer-wins cache entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init is now invoked synchronously inside NewResourceServer, converting previously per-request, per-callsite lazy initialization into a hard construction-time failure. Any transient failure during search index bootstrap (which the code itself documents as potentially slow and now logs a duration for) or watcher setup prevents the resource server from being constructed at all, so the entire process fails startup instead of the previous behavior where only the affected requests returned errors and other operations could proceed; operators on multi-tenant deployments get an all-or-nothing boot for one tenant's bad index.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly moves initialization from per-RPC callsites to construction time: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure, while the previous `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` checks were removed from `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Read`, `List`, `Watch`, `Search`, `History`, `Origin`, `IsHealthy`, `PutBlob`, and `GetBlob`. Since `Init` performs search index initialization (`s.search.init(ctx)`) and starts the watcher (`s.initWatcher()`), any error there will now prevent server construction/startup rather than surfacing on individual requests. That’s a real, diff-grounded operational/architecture concern, but not inherently a correctness defect because fail-fast startup may be intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] With the Init call removed from History and Origin, these methods dereference s.search with no nil guard, while Search retains an explicit 'search index not configured' check. If NewResourceServer is constructed without a search support configured (a non-error condition per Init, which only initializes search when s.search != nil), History and Origin return a nil-pointer panic / 500 to the API caller instead of the typed 'search index not configured' error the sibling Search endpoint returns — a wrong-shape response on a reachable path.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go, the Init(ctx) calls were removed from History and Origin, and both now unconditionally call s.search.History/Origin without checking s.search != nil. The diff shows Search retains an explicit nil guard (`if s.search == nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("search index not configured") }`). Init itself only initializes search when `s.search != nil`, and NewResourceServer now calls Init during construction but does not guarantee s.search is set. Therefore, constructing a server with `s.search == nil` (a condition explicitly handled by Search) makes History/Origin dereference nil and panic, producing an incorrect/500-style response on a reachable path.
